newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel labour federation to sell Hapoalim stake.
newsitem.headline: Israel labour federation to sell Hapoalim stake.

text.p: Israel's Histadrut labour federation said on Tuesday it expected to sign a deal within 48 hours for the sale of its three percent stake in Bank Hapoalim to a U.S. investor group.
"We are in the process of finalising the deal," said Shmuel Avital, head of the Histadrut's finance and economics division.
The group is headed by Jeffrey Keil, who recently left his job as president of Republic New York Corp to form an investment partnership.
Sources close to the negotiations said the price was expected to be around 170 million shekels, slightly above the current value of Hapoalim's shares on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.

Avital said the Histadrut, which began negotiations two months ago with a number of potential buyers, decided to sell its remaining stake in Israel's largest bank to pay off a 150 million shekel loan.
About 20 percent of Hapoalim is traded on the Tel Aviv stock exchange. The rest of its stock is owned by the government.

Keil has joined a group of investors headed by Israeli businessman Eliezer Fishman who are trying to buy a controlling interest in Hapoalim from the government. The group includes U.S. based Reliance Insurance and Bear Stearns.

The Fishman group is the only bidder for the Hapoalim stake. A group headed by Claridge Israel, the investment arm of Canadian billionaire Charles Bronfman, announced in August that it was no longer interested in purchasing the controlling stake.
